items.description: arXiv:2611.28202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. items.description: arXiv:2611.28263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems perform strongly on native-English benchmarks, yet their accuracy degrades sharply when the input speech comes from under represented non-native accents. items.description: arXiv:2611.28314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abliteration is a widely used white-box attack against the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs). items.description: arXiv:2611.28135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large vision-language models can extract personally identifiable information from images, making privacy protection essential for their deployment in perception-oriented tasks. items.description: arXiv:2611.28158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks.
